/staticQuestions/0/answer.source_en: Three core sites. The 3rd Infiltration Tunnel: a 1,635 meter underground passage discovered in 1978 that North Korea built toward Seoul. The ⟦G0⟧: the only civilian-accessible viewpoint into the North, where you can see Kaesong city, the propaganda village, and the Kijongdong flag. Imjingak Peace Park: the 1972 memorial park with the Mangbaedan Altar, the Bridge of Freedom rebuilt 1953, and the bullet-ridden steam locomotive. Photography rules vary by stop and the guide will brief you.

/staticQuestions/0/question.source_en: What can I actually see at the DMZ on this route?

/staticQuestions/1/answer.source_en: Yes — every guest, including infants, must carry their physical passport. Korean ID is checked at the Unification Bridge military checkpoint before entering the DMZ proper. A passport copy or a photo on your phone is not accepted. Without the physical passport the tour will have to skip the DMZ portion and the standard refund policy applies.

/staticQuestions/2/answer.source_en: The 3rd Infiltration Tunnel route closes on Mondays for maintenance. On Mondays the operator usually substitutes the 2nd Infiltration Tunnel if the South Korean military allows access; if not, the route runs as DMZ-without-tunnel, with extended time at Imjingak, the ⟦G0⟧, and Gamaksan. Confirm your travel date with the operator if a Monday is required.

/staticQuestions/2/question.source_en: Can I do this tour on a Monday?

/staticQuestions/3/answer.source_en: The 3rd Tunnel descent is the most physically demanding section of the day. The walk down is fine for most travelers. The climb back up the steep, slippery 350 meter ramp takes about 10-20 minutes and requires moderate fitness. There's a monorail option for an extra fee (about 9,200 KRW round-trip) for visitors with knee, heart, or claustrophobia concerns. Helmets are provided at the entrance.

/staticQuestions/3/question.source_en: How tough is the 3rd Tunnel descent?

/staticQuestions/4/answer.source_en: DMZ access is governed by the South Korean military and can change at short notice for drills, weather, or security reasons. If access is cancelled on the day, the driver-guide substitutes Dorasan Station (when accessible), the Bridge of Freedom plus Mangbaedan extended visit, or extra time at Gamaksan. Refunds are not issued in this case as the route still runs with substitutions; the substitution policy is documented at booking.

/staticQuestions/4/question.source_en: What if military operations cancel DMZ access on the day?

/staticQuestions/5/answer.source_en: Photography is freely allowed at Imjingak Peace Park and Gamaksan. At the ⟦G0⟧, photos toward South Korea are fine, but photos toward North Korea are restricted to the marked yellow line on the open roof level. Inside the 3rd Infiltration Tunnel, photography is forbidden — phones and cameras must stay in the lockers at the entrance. Guide will brief on the rules at each stop.

/staticQuestions/5/question.source_en: Is photography allowed at every stop?

/staticQuestions/6/answer.source_en: Yes — it covers the most distinctive stops in the area in a single balanced day.

/staticQuestions/6/question.source_en: Is this a good choice for first-time visitors to Paju (Seoul Day Trip)?

/staticQuestions/7/answer.source_en: An active day with several walking-heavy stops. Imjingak Peace Park is easy flat walking with a few light steps to the steam-locomotive memorial. The 3rd Infiltration Tunnel is a 350 meter steep ramp descent and ascent — the climb back up is the most physically demanding moment of the day. ⟦G0⟧ has stairs to the open roof. Gamaksan Suspension Bridge requires a 10-40 minute uphill trail walk depending on the entry point.

/staticQuestions/8/answer.source_en: Yes for families whose kids can handle the heavy historical content and physical sections. The 3rd Tunnel is restricted to children who can walk independently and follow safety rules; infants in carriers are not permitted due to the helmet requirement. Younger children find the day emotionally heavy. Gamaksan and the Imjingak gondola are the lighter highlights for kids.

/staticQuestions/8/question.source_en: Is this tour suitable for families?

/staticQuestions/9/answer.source_en: Recommended only for active seniors comfortable with stairs, uneven ground, and a 350 meter steep tunnel ramp. The Imjingak Peace Gondola substitutes for the tunnel descent if needed. ⟦G0⟧ has elevators to most levels. Gamaksan's shorter trail entry (10 minutes) is preferred for senior groups; the driver-guide will route accordingly.

/staticQuestions/10/answer.source_en: Age 10+ recommended. The tour involves heavy historical content, a steep tunnel descent (children get tired on the climb back), suspension-bridge heights at Gamaksan, and a long day overall. Younger children can join but expect emotional and physical fatigue. Babies in carriers cannot enter the 3rd Tunnel due to height and helmet-safety rules.
